proposals.evidence: DEDR5535 gives Kodagu bērï, Malayalam vēr and Tamil vēr root. Survey bērə/vērə preserve their final vowels and match the same botanical sense; source cognacy independently identifies the article. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3633 explicitly gives Tamil/Malayalam nākku and Toda nōf tongue; survey nākkə/nākə and nōf preserve their spellings. Betta Kurumba nelgi is a comparative extension toward the nālage/nālige series documented in Kannada, explicitly only a look-alike in the source. This does not treat the Betta form as a literal DEDR attestation. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: Full DEDR1524 explicitly gives Tamil kiṭa lie down/rest. Survey keḍə is a comparative vowel/stop-transcription variant in the same recumbent sense, discovered through the actual homepage lie search. The existing *kōḍ- (?) parent’s reconstruction uncertainty remains visible for review; this does not endorse the article’s questioned Malto comparison. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
